places.text: Lion, leopard, elephant, buffalo and rhino, plus the largest elephant herds left in East Africa.
places.title: The Big Five, and Then Some

places.text: Calving on the southern plains in February, the Grumeti in June, the Mara river in August — the circuit never stops.
places.title: Following the Migration

places.text: The highest free-standing mountain on earth: rainforest, moorland, alpine desert and glacier in five days of walking.
places.title: Kilimanjaro, 5,895 m

places.text: Six days up the Machame route, one very long night to the summit, and a sunrise you have to earn.
places.title: Uhuru Peak by Machame

places.text: The atoll off the northeast tip of Zanzibar, plus kite surfing at Paje and diving at Pemba.
places.title: Snorkelling Mnemba

places.text: Eighty metres of cold water through Chagga coffee farms on the lower slopes, an easy walk from Moshi.
places.title: Materuni, Under Kilimanjaro

places.text: Flamingo and tree-climbing lions at Manyara; the Rufiji braiding through Nyerere, the largest park in Africa.
places.title: Manyara and the Rufiji

places.text: White sand, warm shallow water and dhows still built by hand on the beach at Nungwi.
places.title: Zanzibar, Nungwi to Paje

places.text: A collapsed caldera twenty kilometres across with its own permanent population of thirty thousand animals.
places.title: The Ngorongoro Crater

places.text: The Udzungwa scarp holds species found nowhere else; Jozani holds the red colobus, also found nowhere else.
places.title: Udzungwa and Jozani

places.text: Cattle-keepers on the northern plains, coffee farmers on the mountain, and a coast that has always faced east.
places.title: Maasai, Chagga, Swahili

places.text: One of the last hunter-gatherer peoples in Africa, speaking a click language unrelated to anything nearby.
places.title: The Hadzabe of Lake Eyasi

places.text: Cloves and cardamom from the Zanzibar plantations, grilled seafood at Forodhani, and ugali everywhere else.
places.title: Spice, Ugali, Urojo

places.text: Four days of live music from across the continent inside the old Arab fort in Stone Town, every February.
places.title: Sauti za Busara

places.text: Enamel-bright Tingatinga painting from Dar es Salaam, and Makonde ebony carving from the southern plateau.
places.title: Tingatinga and Makonde

places.text: Stone Town is UNESCO-listed; Kilwa Kisiwani was the richest port on the Swahili coast six centuries ago.
places.title: Stone Town and Kilwa

places.text: Olduvai Gorge holds the earliest human record; the coast holds a thousand years of Indian Ocean trade.
places.title: Olduvai and the Coast

places.text: Harbour of peace: the ferry terminal, the fish market at Kivukoni, and the dhows still working the channel.
places.title: Dar es Salaam

places.text: Brass-studded Indian doors and carved Omani frames, on coral-rag houses in alleys too narrow to drive.
places.title: The Doors of Stone Town

places.text: Minibuses inland, dhows on the water, and a fish auction at Kivukoni that starts before it is light.
places.title: Dala Dalas and Dhows

places.text: Maasai boma visits on the crater rim road, and Chagga coffee walks on the lower slopes of Kilimanjaro.
places.title: Boma and Coffee Farm

places.text: Mobile camps that follow the migration, and beach houses on the Zanzibar east coast with nothing either side.
places.title: Camps and Spice Islands

places.text: The conservation area is the rare model where Maasai pastoralists and wildlife legally use the same land.
places.title: Ngorongoro, Shared Ground

places.text: The Serengeti kopjes at the end of the day, and the migration column stretching past the edge of the frame.
places.title: Acacia, Kopje, Sunset

places.text: The south and west: huge elephant populations, hippo crowded into shrinking pools, and no other vehicles.
places.title: Ruaha and Katavi

places.text: Summit Africa's highest mountain, cross the Serengeti and sleep on the Indian Ocean, in the same fortnight.
places.title: Mountain, Plain and Reef
